wins.text: Onsite signings of 107 in Q2 with active sites reaching 1,934, up 12% YoY, approaching 2,000 active Onsites
FMI Technology installed base grew to 119,000 weighted devices, up 11% YoY; 7,188 devices signed in Q2 (112/day vs. prior target of 100/day); ~42% of sales now flowing through FMI
eBusiness rose ~25% YoY driven by eProcurement; digital footprint reached 59.4% of sales, hitting 60% in June
Operating cash flow of $258M in Q2 2024 at 88% of net income, above historical Q2 conversion rates; debt reduced to 6.3% of total capital from 9.4% a year ago
National account contracts growing at low double digits with improved mix; core accounts per day up ~7% YoY in H1 2024 vs. down ~4% in H1 2023

risks.text: Net sales grew only ~2% YoY and EPS fell 2% to $0.51 from $0.52; sub-50 ISM for 19 of the last 20 months creating persistent industrial headwind on 75% of revenue
Operating margin declined 80 bps YoY to 20.2%; gross margin down 40 bps to 45.1% due to product/customer mix and negative pricing of 30-60 bps including slippage in non-fastener/safety categories

Regional leadership reporting uptick in customer layoffs, shift reductions, and extended holiday shutdowns; customers 'throwing in the towel' on near-term and cutting costs, suggesting demand weakness may persist
Pricing discipline flagged as insufficient in safety and other non-fastener product categories; price/cost turned nearly neutral vs. modestly positive in Q1 2024

Mature Onsites experiencing low-single-digit revenue declines as heavily manufacturing-weighted customer base contracts; uncertainty around July impact from Texas hurricane and extended holiday shutdowns

guidance_items.detail: Full-year net capex raised to $235M-$255M range, up $10M from prior range, driven by hub automation, Utah DC upgrade, FMI spend, and IT purchases
Q3 gross margin expected to be roughly in line with Q2 seasonality or slightly better as warehousing ramp costs largely contained to Q2; pricing discipline actions being taken in Q3
Digital footprint target for full year 2024 revised down to ~63% from prior ~66% expectation due to lower customer spending volumes
No specific revenue guidance given; management expects H2 2024 to benefit from strong H1 signings activity barring further macro erosion, but no quantitative target provided

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Pricing deflation spreading beyond fasteners into safety and other non-fastener product categories — management did not proactively disclose the safety/other pricing slippage
Competitive dynamics driving price concessions — whether margin pressure was offensive (share grab) or defensive (competitor pressure) was not addressed in prepared remarks
Election-related demand uncertainty causing customers to hold capital spending — regional feedback on election-driven hesitancy was not mentioned proactively
